title.justification: The title provides a succinct and precise description of the core subject of the paper, focusing on the application of the GRAND decoding technique to Rayleigh fading communication channels.

extractions.description: The paper explores the application of Guessing Random Additive Noise Decoding (GRAND) to Rayleigh fading channels, introducing a variant called Fading-GRAND. This approach adapts Test Error Patterns (TEP) generation to handle multipath frequency non-selective Rayleigh fading, improving the performance of channel code decoders.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper discusses advancements in wireless communication decoding technology, it does not explicitly focus on climate or ecological sustainable development themes. It is more aligned with technology improvement in communication systems.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: GRAND is a universal Maximum likelihood decoding technique for high-rate and short-length channel codes. These short codes are appealing for ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC).

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper lies in advancements within the field of communication technology, with no direct implications or discussions on climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: In this work, we extend the application of GRAND to multipath frequency non-selective Rayleigh fading communication channels.

secondary_categories.quote: Fading-GRAND adapts the TEP generation to the fading conditions of the channel, outperforming traditional channel code decoders.
